trajectory.thought: The leader is a seeded baseline (trimmed_mean on pool1) and the runner-up margin is statistically indistinguishable. Per the stopping rule, I should accept it. The series has strong trend and seasonality with moderate ranking stability; the trimmed mean over the 5 most consistent models (ARIMA, ETS, THETA, CWT_catboost, NaiveSeasonal) already captures the complementary strengths while trimming the outlier-prone NaiveSeasonal, which is well-suited to this non-stationary, seasonally structured series.

action_args.justification: Strong trend (0.96) and seasonality (0.77) with moderate ranking stability (Kendall tau 0.368) favour a robust trimmed mean over the 5 most consistently ranked models. The trimmed mean already discards the weakest contributor (NaiveSeasonal) while retaining the complementary ARIMA/ETS/THETA/CWT_catboost group. The runner-up is statistically indistinguishable, and with only 3 validation windows further weight-fitting would chase noise rather than signal.
